steps.title: Publish a standalone clock page at docs/index.html
steps.intent: Create a single self-contained static HTML page at docs/index.html that, when opened in a browser, computes the current time from the browser clock and renders it as an ISO 8601 date-time string under the exact heading "Current time". It is served as-is by GitHub Pages (main / docs) with no build step, bundler, or workflow. This is the operator's own product page, not the oversight dashboard or any installed machinery.
steps.acceptance: docs/index.html exists, starts with an HTML5 doctype, and contains the exact heading text "Current time". When loaded in a browser it computes the current time client-side from the system clock (not a hardcoded value) and renders it as a valid ISO 8601 date-time string that matches the viewer's clock at render time — never empty, a UNIX epoch, or a non-ISO format, and never in the future. The page is a single standalone file needing no build step, bundler, or workflow to serve, and nothing is written outside docs/.
steps.stand_in: ISO 8601 rendered from the browser Date API and displayed in the operator's local timezone with UTC offset at second precision (e.g. "2026-08-25T11:30:00-04:00"), grounded in runbooks/domain-expert/common.md ("Timestamps display in the operator's local timezone") and pending the operator's answer to q-iso-format (the alternative is UTC 'Z' via toISOString(), e.g. "2026-08-25T15:30:00Z"). A single timestamp is captured once at page render (no live ticking), which satisfies #40's "at render time" acceptance.

verification_targets.check: docs/index.html exists and its first line is an HTML5 doctype (<!DOCTYPE html>, case-insensitive).
verification_targets.run: test -f docs/index.html && head -n1 docs/index.html | grep -iqE '^[[:space:]]*<!doctype html>'

verification_targets.check: docs/index.html contains the exact heading text "Current time".

The page computes the timestamp client-side from the browser clock (uses the JavaScript Date API at load) rather than embedding a fixed literal, guaranteeing the rendered value matches the viewer's clock at render time and is never a hardcoded UNIX epoch. The ISO 8601 shape of the rendered string is confirmed on render per q-iso-format.
The page is a single self-contained file: docs/index.html embeds its clock logic inline in a <script> block, so GitHub Pages on main/docs serves it with no build step or bundler.

boundary_cases.description: If the browser Date API is unavailable or yields an invalid value, the page must not render an empty string, a UNIX epoch, or a non-ISO value; it shows a fallback message instead.
The timestamp is captured per page load; reloading across the local midnight boundary yields the correct next-day ISO date (no stale date carried over).
Opened directly via GitHub Pages (main / docs) with no build step, bundler, or server-side rendering, the page still computes and displays the timestamp entirely client-side.
